
  P2 — the hit target fell from 38×44 to 16px. I'd have shipped Greg a smaller target than the one he complained about, on
  a phone. Reused the floor that already exists — min-height: 2.5rem under (pointer: coarse), the dock's number — as
  tw:pointer-coarse:min-h-10, on all three controls, per narrow-window.css's own argument that a floor given to one
  control is a bug filed about the one beside it. Verified under mobile emulation where (pointer: coarse) genuinely
  matches (hasTouch alone doesn't flip it): all three at exactly 40px.

  One non-code correction: my plan doc said the unfindability was the bug. That states an inference about Greg's
  experience as an observation — he filed from an article, phrased it as placement, and never said he'd looked and failed.
  Now separated into what was measured and what was read into it.

  It cleared the two things I was least sure of: FEEDBACK_TRIGGER_SELECTOR isn't circular (renaming a hook and its class
  together is harmless drift, not a false green), and the safe-area line is "justified, not scope creep".

  Still to do: full suite, push to dev, resolve the Sentry issue, worktree:check before removal.
